title: Why Do We Root for Other Players? | Designing Games Worth Watching

scenes.title: Who are you watching?
lines: Several animals are jumping at once. In this Ultimate Chicken Horse clip, who are you watching?
Follow the chicken. Will it avoid the saw and reach the next platform? You start looking for different actions in the same view.
Now watch Gang Beasts. Choose one of the bodies grabbing and hanging on, and look for where that character is still holding.
These short shots show different situations. Follow the next action of the character you chose.
Next is the developer’s early truck-level gameplay. Characters move and grapple on two trucks. Pick one to follow in your mind.
Choosing whom to watch does not change the rules. It changes which movement you look for first and what you want to see happen next.
Using footage from these two actual games, we will separate recognition cues, a reason to care, and a view that makes important moments readable.

scenes.title: Following through overlap
lines: Watch this Ultimate Chicken Horse developer recording. A robot-costumed monkey and a rabbit wearing a hat differ in shape. Look for those differences as they jump.
Appearance helps you find the same animal after the group separates toward different platforms. Remembering only its screen position can become confusing.
Now watch the Gang Beasts truck level. In this early version, the bodies have similar shapes but different colors. Follow the cyan character.
As characters approach each other and the camera turns, remembering the left side is not enough. Also track which truck and which nearby character connect to the participant.
A body moving below the roof does not immediately end the action. Look for a hand still at the edge. Reading an identity and following its action are different tasks.
This is not a controlled experiment. We are observing what clues appearance, color and surrounding positions offer.
Check whether the same participant can be found on a small screen or in a crowd. A marker must be readable with the moving body.

scenes.title: Choose someone and watch
lines: On the window-cleaning scaffold in Gang Beasts, choose red or yellow. Standing on the platform and hanging below it lead to different immediate actions.
Following yellow can raise the question of getting back up; following red can raise the question of maintaining its grip. The same view supports different questions.
Now watch another attempt on the trucks. Cyan and yellow come together while green moves nearby. Look first for the hands and body of the participant you chose.
A body tilting while held can give a viewer a reason to hope it stays aboard. The visible posture offers a question about the next move without a long character biography.
You can choose a different character in the next attempt. This means deciding whom to follow, not adding a new game feature.
Do not infer a player’s personality from one action. Start by describing the movement you can actually see.
The view can provide room for a small expectation. Whether people actually enjoy watching more still needs to be checked with viewers.

scenes.title: What is at risk right now?
lines: Return to the window-cleaning scaffold. A body can hang below while a hand remains attached to the edge. Watch the relationship between the hand and platform.
The open space below makes the danger legible. A gripping hand and the next foothold may matter more to this moment than a large set of statistics.
Switch to early Ultimate Chicken Horse gameplay. Watch the moving saw alongside the chicken’s jump. The danger lies between takeoff and the next platform.
The horse moves in a different attempt. The cut should not make its outcome look like a continuation of the chicken’s jump.
The same relationship appears at the side of a truck. Seeing the roof, hanging body and road below helps explain why that grip matters.
The next attempt brings them together on the roof again. Follow who holds whom and which edge they approach.
A tight crop can lose the next space, while a very wide view can lose hands and bodies. Check whether the participant and immediate risk remain connected in the view.

scenes.title: Keep track as the view changes
lines: In this space-themed Ultimate Chicken Horse gameplay, choose a moving animal. Follow its rising body, propulsion flames and nearby rocks together.
The framing changes as the animals spread apart. Seeing the overall space and quickly finding the animal you were following are different tasks.
Look for the same appearance in the next view. Watching only the center because the animal was there earlier can make you follow someone else.
Flames beneath the feet and nearby rocks help reveal movement direction. After recognizing the participant, read where it is going and what it will encounter next.
Distinguish approaching the flag from rising again. Edited attempts should not be read as one continuous flight.
We are observing visible movement and framing, not discovering the internal camera algorithm or the best view for everyone.
Check whether the chosen participant can be found after a framing change. Even an attractive view should preserve the next action.

scenes.title: An understandable result, even in defeat
lines: Finally, watch cyan and yellow on the truck. Follow the sequence of grappling, a body tilting, and the distance between them changing.
The standing position alone does not settle the outcome. A character may rise after falling over or keep a hand attached after moving below the roof.
When both bodies descend at the edge, follow which contacts remain. A large label for the favored participant cannot communicate that process by itself.
Next is a separate scaffold scene. Watch how the hanging characters and platform angle change.
Follow the red character through the shot. Distinguishing a remaining grip from a falling body connects the visible outcome with the action that produced it.
This material does not establish the whole match’s winner. We describe only the attempts and falls shown.
Connect the selected participant, the action attempted and the outcome actually verified. That connection should be readable before adding a large call to cheer.
